title: CsvHelper
tagline: A CSV reader and writer for .NET, built for speed.
description: CsvHelper is a SIMD accelerated, allocation free CSV reader and strict RFC 4180 writer for .NET 10, .NET Standard 2.0 and 2.1 and .NET Framework 4.7.

guides.title: Target frameworks
guides.description: What differs between the .NET 10, .NET Standard and .NET Framework 4.7 builds.

guides.title: Performance
guides.description: How the reader and writer are fast: UTF-8 throughout, 64-byte SIMD blocks, branch-free quotes and more.

guides.title: Benchmarks
guides.description: CsvHelper against Sep and Sylvan.Data.Csv, measured with BenchmarkDotNet.

guides.title: Building and testing
guides.description: Build the library and run its tests.

features.title: SIMD parsing
features.text: Parses UTF-8 directly with AVX-512, AVX2 or 128-bit vectors, finds quoted regions branch-free and exposes fields as zero-copy spans.

features.title: Allocation free
features.text: Fields are spans into the reader's buffer and strings are created only when you ask for one, so reading a file field by field allocates a few kilobytes however large it is. The writer allocates a few hundred bytes.

features.title: Every core
features.text: ParallelEnumerate maps records on several threads and returns them in input order. ParallelWriteRecords formats records on every core and writes exactly what WriteRecords would.

features.title: Source-generated records
features.text: A source generator in the package writes the code that reads and writes [CsvRecord] types at compile time: no reflection, as fast as hand-written code, and mapping mistakes are compile errors.

features.title: Native AOT and trimming
features.text: On .NET 10 both packages are marked AOT compatible and trimmable, and the analyzers check them on every build. Only C#'s dynamic and LINQ queries need code generated at run time.

features.title: Async throughout
features.text: ReadAsync, await foreach, GetRecordsAsync, and WriteRecordsAsync for IAsyncEnumerable. Reads wait only when the buffer needs refilling and otherwise complete without allocating.

features.title: Strict RFC 4180 output
features.text: By default: CRLF, minimal quoting, doubled quotes and consistent field counts, with numbers formatted straight into a UTF-8 buffer.

features.title: More than RFC 4180
features.text: Also reads and writes escaped files (the old Linux mode), unescaped files and fixed-width files.

features.title: Adapts to messy files
features.text: Detects the separator and encoding, recovers from stray quotes and has explicit options for malformed data.

features.title: LINQ
features.text: CsvHelper.Linq queries CSV with any LINQ operator, reads only the columns and rows a query uses, and joins with Entity Framework Core by sending it only the keys it needs.

features.title: Fast dynamic records
features.text: No record type? Dynamic records hold their fields' bytes rather than a dictionary of strings, and bind each member to its column once: 16 to 22x faster than ExpandoObject.

features.title: Highly configurable
features.text: Attributes and record maps fit columns to your types, even types you can't change, and the reader and writer options cover separators, quoting, headers, cultures and more.

features.title: Fast, exact numbers
features.text: Floats parse with a port of fast_float and format with a port of Dragonbox: bit-identical to .NET's own results, checked on all 2^32 floats, and 3 to 4.5x faster.

features.title: Safe with untrusted files
features.text: Escapes spreadsheet formulas such as =1+2, caps record size so an unclosed quote cannot fill memory, and can keep field values out of exception messages.

features.title: Every .NET
features.text: .NET 10 with SIMD, plus .NET Standard 2.0 and 2.1 and .NET Framework 4.7, which read and write exactly the same CSV.

features.title: Fuzz tested
features.text: The reader is fuzzed against an independent reference parser at every vector width, from every input source and with tiny buffers. Tests run on .NET 10, .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8.

features.title: Measured
features.text: Benchmarked against Sep and Sylvan.Data.Csv with BenchmarkDotNet, with every library returning the same results.

features.title: Open source
features.text: Free for commercial use and dual licensed under MS-PL and Apache 2.0. Many contributors have helped make CsvHelper what it is.

contributors.intro: Want to contribute? Great! Here are a few guidelines.
guidelines: If you want to do a feature, post an issue about the feature first. Some features are intentionally left out, some features may already be in the works, or I may have some advice on how I think it should be done. I would feel bad if time was spent on some code that won't be used.
If you want to do a bug fix, it might not be a bad idea to post about it too. I've had the same bug fixed by multiple people at the same time before.

All code should have a unit test. If you make a feature, there should be significant tests around the feature. If you do a bug fix, there should be a test specific to that bug so it doesn't happen again.
Pull requests should have a single commit. If you have multiple commits, squash them into a single commit before requesting a pull.
When in Rome: Try and follow the code styling already in place. I use default Visual Studio Text Editor settings but change tabs to Keep tabs.
